route: 5/8 (simplex: correlation decay with presentation distance, replicated across both studies)
evidence: Route 5/8 variant: a simplex (correlation-decays-with-presentation-distance) test on the live data, n=8,475 rows / 4 items (ANX1 n=2549 mean 3.053, ANX2 n=847 mean 3.156, ANX3 n=2536 mean 3.013, ANX4 n=2543 mean 2.899). The four items are near-synonymous affect words (nervous / uneasy / tense / bothered), so no content, marker-item or range route separates them; means span only 0.26 and all six correlations lie in 0.85-0.92, so means are not usable as identifiers either. What IS testable is the adjacency structure: only three distinct orderings of four items exist up to reversal, and mean correlation by lag is monotone decreasing for exactly one of them -- the shipped order 1-2-3-4 (lag1 0.9138 > lag2 0.8964 > lag3 0.8554), against 1-3-2-4 (0.9046, 0.9101, 0.8554; lag2 exceeds lag1) and 1-2-4-3 (0.9037, 0.8883, 0.9018; lag3 exceeds lag2). It replicates within Study 1 alone, n=847 (0.9157 / 0.8968 / 0.8692), and within the independent Study 2 sample, n=1,702, where ANX2 was dropped upstream so only the distance-3 prediction survives: r(ANX1,ANX4)=0.8475 against r(ANX1,ANX3)=0.9015 (distance 2) and r(ANX3,ANX4)=0.8974 (distance 1). NOT ESTABLISHED: the simplex is symmetric under reversal, so it cannot rule out ANX1='bothered'...ANX4='nervous'; the gaps it turns on are 0.02-0.06; and it does not pin any single item's identity independently of the sequence. Hence PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.

route: per-item n fingerprint against the raw source spreadsheets (core model 3) + content-predicted correlation structure (route 8)
evidence: Live per-item n from irw_table_sets: COMP1 2547, COMP2 847, COMP3 2534, COMP4 2540, COMP5 2545. Re-deriving the processing filter (AttentionCheck==2, numeric resp in 1-7, Study 2 COMP2 dropped) over S1 Data (.s004, n=847) and S4 Data (.s007, n=1702) reproduces 2547/847/2534/2540/2545 exactly -- all five distinct, so every live code is tied to one specific spreadsheet column. Column->appendix-wording: Study 1 correlations make COMP2-COMP4 the single largest off-diagonal (0.914, next highest 0.853), as predicted by appendix items 2 and 4 being near-paraphrases, and COMP5 the weakest with the rest (mean r 0.716 vs 0.783-0.826), as predicted by item 5 being the only 'being compared' rather than 'competing' item. This does NOT separate COMP2 from COMP4, nor COMP1 from COMP3 (both 'value/importance of competition' phrasings); those two positions rest on appendix presentation order alone. Hence PARTIAL.

route: 3 (published totals: the paper's Study 1 t-test on MISTRUST = mean(8 - TRUSTn)) for the option_text<->resp axis; routes 1-9 all unavailable for the item_text<->item axis, route 8 attempted and rejected
evidence: Two axes, different outcomes. option_text<->resp VERIFIED: the study's SPSS syntax (S3 Data, line 142) defines MISTRUST = MEAN(8-TRUST1, 8-TRUST2, 8-TRUST3, 8-TRUST4), and recomputing the paper's Study 1 condition test on that composite from the raw PLOS spreadsheets reproduces it exactly: t(845) = 3.318 vs published 3.32, 95% CI [0.14, 0.53] vs published [0.14, 0.53], d = 0.228 vs published 0.23, M(HRC) = 3.527 (n=414) vs M(LRC) = 3.192 (n=433). The flipped-anchor counterfactual gives HRC 4.473 vs LRC 4.808, difference -0.335, the opposite sign, so 1 = 'Not at all' ... 7 = 'Completely' is the only direction consistent with the paper. The reconstruction is tied to the live table without an export: per-item n from the raw files is 2547 / 2544 / 2542 / 2547 for TRUST1-4 against irw_table_sets' 2547 / 2544 / 2542 / 2547, difference 0 for all four. item_text<->item NOT ESTABLISHED: the codes ARE the source column names, but the appendix lists its four sentences unnumbered, so sentence-to-code rests on presentation order alone and no route can test it -- one shared 1-7 scale (route 2), one unidimensional block with no published subscale or per-item statistics (routes 1, 3, 5), no reverse-worded or marker item (routes 6, 7), no implied parameter (route 4), integers not labels in the source (route 9). Route 8 attempted and rejected as post-hoc: means TRUST1 4.560, TRUST2 4.325, TRUST3 4.534, TRUST4 4.348 group {1,3} above {2,4}, consistent with the appendix order's character-vs-trust wording split but matched by a random pairing 1 time in 3 and separating neither pair internally; correlations r(2,3)=0.870, r(2,4)=0.877, r(3,4)=0.879, r(1,*)=0.768-0.799 distinguish nothing. Hence PARTIAL: the response-option direction is pinned for all four items, the order of the four sentences among the four codes is not.

route: source data-file labels (exemption) + route 9-style keyed-response matching against published CTT P-values
evidence: Live table via irw_fetch (20 items x 190 respondents); re-runnable as verify_gpt4mcq_young_2025.R. mapping_basis is data_labels so this step is formally exempt, but the deposit publishes a SECOND, different 20-item AI set under the same AIQ1-AIQ20 codes, so the two candidates were tested against the paper's own published CTT P-values (Supplementary Materials 3). Under the shipped .sav labels the keyed answer is value 1 for all 20 items and P(resp==1) matches the published P-value item for item: 0.916/0.916, 0.889/0.889, 0.816/0.816, 0.926/0.926, 0.911/0.911, 0.937/0.937, 0.932/0.932, 0.932/0.932, 0.926/0.926, 0.889/0.889, 0.889/0.889, 0.926/0.926, 0.947/0.947, 0.679/0.679, 0.832/0.832, 0.926/0.926, 0.937/0.937, 0.937/0.937, 0.500/0.500, 0.868/0.868 -- largest deviation 0.0005. Under the Supplementary Materials 2 wording the keyed position would attract a mean of 0.103 of respondents (0.011-0.100 for 18 of 20 items; the two exceptions, AIQ5 and AIQ19, are the items whose SM2 key also sits at position 1). WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH on its own: the published P-values tie across items (0.926 four times, 0.937 three times, 0.889 three times), so this route alone cannot separate those items from each other. What separates them is that the stem label, the option labels and the responses are all carried on the SAME .sav column and the IRW code IS that column name (data/gpt4mcq_young_2025.r selects starts_with('AIQ') and never renames), so no permutation is possible -- the numeric check is what rules out the rival wording set, not what assigns codes to text.

Route 9 response-frequency matching, .sav labels vs live integers, all 15 items x 5 levels = 75 cells, 0 mismatches: e.g. Q23e_Fear_of_needles 308,109,94,79,122 raw vs 308,109,94,79,122 live; Q23h_Risk_men_HPV 180,29,40,58,46 vs 180,29,40,58,46; Q23n_New_partner_condom 12,15,40,99,483 vs 12,15,40,99,483. All 15 count-vectors are distinct (0 duplicates), so the route separates every item from every other, and no permutation of the 5 levels reproduces the match, which confirms the script's reversal of the .sav's own 1='Totally agree'..5='Totally disagree' coding into IRW 1='Totally disagree'..5='Totally agree'. What it does NOT establish is the WORDING: item_text is the .sav variable labels, the study's English for a Swedish-administered form, and no data check can validate a translation.

route: item x resp cell-count identity between the CC BY 4.0 OSF deposit's own data set columns and the live table, plus permutation discrimination and the authors' rename()/recode statements
evidence: BLOCKED on rights, nothing shipped, so no item_text<->item or option_text<->resp mapping exists in the corpus to verify; status NO_ROUTE follows the batch_026/027 convention for blocked tables rather than reflecting an absence of evidence.
